source_acquisition.search_note: The inventory candidate and the PDF p.19 hyperlink resolve to the same public repository. gh metadata and README title/citation verify the paper relationship; the repository tree has experiment scripts plus partial rendered assets but no paper TeX or complete figure/table plotting scripts. Website-only assets and unmatched Appendix Figure 5–11 composites were not promoted to exact visual sources. The result is partial_visual_source rather than repository_without_visual_source because Figure 1 and several components/table blocks are directly present.

paper_style.palette_strategy: A small repeated categorical vocabulary (blue, green, red, orange, purple) distinguishes models, dimensions, batch sizes and raw/whitened states; pale fills and gray dashed boundaries provide secondary regime cues.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figures 1–5 are primarily embedded raster composites; Figures 6–11 combine embedded raster distributions with PDF/text resources; Tables 1–2 are predominantly vector text and rules.
paper_style.style_consistency: Times-like body/captions and bold caption titles are stable. Handwritten chart labels recur across the paper, but raster versus mixed construction and local color semantics vary; grayscale-safe redundancy is limited.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Illustration. Contrastive learning yields (approximately) Gaussian representations.

color.semantic_mapping: Thumbnail images indicate input views; orange/blue curves indicate two view paths; slate block is the contrastive learning pipeline; pale-blue sphere and output thumbnails indicate the Gaussian-distribution endpoint.

encodings.text: Image/View, Contrastive learning pipeline, Gaussian Distribution

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual illustration only; no sample count, numeric scale, statistical estimate, or uncertainty. Two augmented-view groups feed a contrastive-learning block and a spherical Gaussian-distribution metaphor.
figures.evidence_relation: Connects the introduction's actual-distribution question to the alignment/uniformity objective and the Gaussian-projection predictions tested in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–2.
design_strengths: The causal direction is immediately legible.
Separate colored paths distinguish the two views without a legend.
The output label preserves the paper's approximately-qualified headline.
design_weaknesses: The spherical Gaussian metaphor can imply an exact finite-dimensional joint Gaussian law.
Normalized versus unnormalized representations and fixed-k asymptotic conditions are not shown.
Raster handwritten text and photo thumbnails scale poorly and have low grayscale robustness.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a three-stage horizontal pipeline with explicit input, mechanism, and output labels; keep the caption's approximation qualifier visible.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Uniformity vs. alignment across settings. A simple linear encoder trained on synthetic Laplace data exhibits (i) near-optimal alignment across all configurations and (ii) steadily improving uniformity as batch size or dimensionality grow.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue gradient encodes increasingly uniform negative-pair distributions; green encodes positive-pair alignment; pale blue/green fills and gray dashed envelopes mark the visual ranges.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: lower right in each of the two main panels

encodings.x: representation dimension in the left panel; batch size in the right panel
encodings.y: cosine similarity for uniformity and alignment
encodings.line: solid distribution outlines and gray dashed envelopes
encodings.facet: left=dimension sweep; right=batch-size sweep; upper=uniformity, lower=alignment
encodings.text: less uniform, more uniform, consistent optimal alignment, uniformity, alignment

figures.data_and_statistics: Synthetic Laplace data with a simple linear encoder. Positive-pair and negative-pair cosine-similarity distributions are compared while dimension or batch size changes. No error bars, seed spread, or sample counts are displayed; violin width carries distribution information.
figures.evidence_relation: Direct empirical interface to Assumption 1 and the §4.1 plateau route; Figures 7–8 repeat the same experiment as histograms. The high alignment/continued uniformity separation is the mechanism evidence.
design_strengths: The two theoretical terms share the same setting axis.
Violin shapes retain distribution information rather than only a mean.
Direct labels and dashed envelopes reduce the lookup burden.
design_weaknesses: Envelope semantics and upper/lower ranges are not defined in the caption.
Repeated legends and handwritten labels consume space.
Distribution width is not tied to n or repeated-run uncertainty.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place complementary mechanism quantities in upper/lower rows under one sweep variable, using direct labels for plateau versus improvement.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Synthetic data experiments. Left: representation norm statistics vs. batch size (curves denote dimension), showing thin-shell concentration with increasing d and N. Top middle/right: norm histograms illustrating radius tightening. Bottom: normality diagnostics (AD, DP), with averages in the Gaussian acceptance range.

color.semantic_mapping: Four colors identify batch sizes in norm histograms and five colors identify representation dimensions in curves; the two legend blocks carry different semantics.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: right margin, with separate upper and lower legends

encodings.x: batch size for curves; norm value for histograms
encodings.y: norm mean, CV, density, AD value, or DP value depending on panel
encodings.color: batch size in histograms; dimension in curves
encodings.facet: 2×3: left radial statistics; middle/right norm distributions and AD/DP diagnostics

figures.data_and_statistics: Synthetic Laplace inputs and linear encoders. Norm mean/CV show radial concentration; top-middle/right histograms show radius tightening at dimensions 32 and 128; bottom-middle/right curves show coordinate-wise AD and DP values across batch size. No uncertainty bands or repeated-seed variation are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Combines the three §5 synthetic predictions—thin shell, coordinate-level Gaussian diagnostics, and dependence on d/N—before Table 1 gives endpoint values for Laplace, GMM, and Binary settings.
design_strengths: Radial and coordinate diagnostics share one compact visual object.
The histograms expose distribution shape beside aggregate curves.
Separate legends preserve batch-size versus dimension semantics.
design_weaknesses: Six panels switch units and scales without panel letters.
Nine categorical colors make cross-panel decoding expensive and weak in grayscale.
Average AD/DP values can conceal coordinate heterogeneity and are easy to overread as joint Gaussian evidence.
figures.reusable_pattern: Arrange global concentration, raw distributions, and test statistics as a 2×3 evidence chain, with a legend block for each independent experimental factor.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: CIFAR-10 training dynamics. A two-layer MLP trained with InfoNCE on CIFAR-10 exhibits increasing Gaussianity over training. Left: representation norms concentrate as indicated by declining CV (Eq. 20). Middle: the AD statistic decreases from non-Gaussian levels into the normal range. Right: the fraction of coordinates passing the DP normality test rises steadily.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue encodes CV, black encodes AD, orange encodes DP passing fraction; red/green background bands encode the AD non-Gaussian/Gaussian threshold regime.

encodings.y: CV, AD value, or DP-passing feature fraction
encodings.color: metric identity and AD threshold regime
encodings.line: solid metric trajectories and one dashed AD threshold

figures.data_and_statistics: CIFAR-10 two-layer ReLU MLP trained with InfoNCE; evaluation follows the test representations through training. CV tracks norm concentration, AD tracks a coordinate-wise normality statistic, and the right panel tracks the fraction of coordinates passing the DP threshold. No error bars or seed distribution are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Extends Figure 3 from controlled synthetic data to realistic contrastive training and supplies the temporal mechanism for Table 1's ResNet-18 endpoint comparison.
design_strengths: A shared epoch axis makes the co-emergence of three diagnostics legible.
The AD threshold band turns a statistic into an explicit decision region.
The three-panel row links radial and coordinate-wise changes.
design_weaknesses: The background decision band can imply a binary Gaussian claim beyond the coordinate-wise test.
Representative-run status and repetition are absent from the graphic.
Different y quantities and units cannot be compared by vertical position across panels.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned time-series panels for a structural metric, a thresholded statistic, and a passing fraction; keep the threshold visible in the same row.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.module: Appendix D exact alignment bound in plateau discussion

caption.text: vMF exponential tilt distribution for different concentration scales kappa (κ).

color.semantic_mapping: Blue points show mass on each sphere, gray wireframes hold the geometry fixed, red axis marks the tilt direction, and black labels identify κ.

encodings.line: sphere mesh and red vertical axis

figures.data_and_statistics: Illustrative vMF angular distributions; κ increases angular concentration around an axis. There is no probability-density scale, sample-size statement, or statistical uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Visualizes Appendix D's stationary-point discussion for the generalized plateau surrogate and complements Figure 2's uniform-sphere mechanism; it is not an empirical Gaussianity test.
design_strengths: Fixed sphere geometry makes concentration the dominant visual change.
Five levels give a clear monotone intuition for κ.
The axis cue connects the drawing to the tilt language in Appendix D.
design_weaknesses: Perspective and point density are a metaphor rather than a calibrated density display.
No axes, colorbar, or quantitative scale define the angular law.
The short caption leaves vMF and the increasing-concentration conclusion to the body text.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use fixed-coordinate small multiples for one theoretical parameter sweep and state explicitly that the object is a schematic.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Thin-shell concentration across pretrained models. Radius distributions of representations from supervised models (DenseNet, ResNet) and contrastive models (CLIP, DINO). All models exhibit thin-shell concentration, with contrastive methods showing tighter clustering (lower CV, Eq. (20)).

color.semantic_mapping: Green marks supervised DenseNet/ResNet, red/pink marks CLIP text/image, blue marks DINO; purple CV annotations and gray group divider are auxiliary.

encodings.shape: filled radius histograms with center line
encodings.line: distribution boundary and dashed center reference
encodings.facet: five models, grouped Supervised versus Contrastive
encodings.text: group labels, model names, CV values

figures.data_and_statistics: MS-COCO validation radius distributions for DenseNet, ResNet, CLIP Text, CLIP Image, and DINO. CV values are .115, .118, .055, .054, and .034 respectively. Histogram shape carries distribution information; there are no error bars, n labels, or repeated-run uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Supports Assumption 2's thin-shell condition and links to Table 2's coordinate diagnostics and Figures 9–10's whitening comparison; it broadens the experiment beyond the exact unimodal InfoNCE setting.
design_strengths: Group divider and direct CV labels make the relative concentration contrast immediate.
Small multiples preserve model identity and a common visual grammar.
The figure pairs naturally with the coordinate-level Table 2.
design_weaknesses: Panel y ranges differ, so peak heights are not cross-model quantities.
No legend or explicit n leaves model/color decoding dependent on direct labels.
Narrow panels crowd model names and CV labels.
figures.reusable_pattern: Group radius histograms by training paradigm and annotate the radial summary directly; use common axes when cross-panel height is meant to be compared.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Alignment and uniformity vs. batch size. Histogram view of cosine similarities for positive pairs (alignment) and negatives (uniformity), corresponding to Fig. 2. As batch size increases, alignment remains high while uniformity improves, with negative-pair similarities concentrating near zero. The middle panel is a zoom of the left; the right panel shows that at very low dimensionality, increasing batch size yields little uniformity gain.

color.semantic_mapping: Five colors encode batch sizes 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128; black arrows/text identify uniformity and alignment.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: right side shared across the three panels

encodings.facet: Dim=512 full view; Dim=512 zoom; Dim=32 low-dimensional view
encodings.text: Dim labels and arrows for uniformity/alignment

figures.data_and_statistics: Positive-pair alignment and negative-pair uniformity cosine-similarity distributions across batch sizes 8–128. The full and zoom views expose the near-one alignment peak and the near-zero negative-pair concentration; the low-dimensional panel preserves a limited-gain boundary. No uncertainty intervals are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix alternate visualization of Figure 2's batch-size sweep; it provides distribution-level evidence for alignment saturation and the low-dimensional exception.
design_strengths: The zoom preserves information hidden by the large alignment spike.
The right panel records a boundary where the headline gain weakens.
A shared legend covers all five batch-size conditions.
design_weaknesses: Overlaid fills obscure the central distributions after many series are combined.
Color is the only batch-size encoding and is weak in grayscale.
No panel letters or sample counts are provided.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a full-range histogram with a targeted zoom and a deliberately limiting condition to show both the mechanism and its boundary.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Alignment and uniformity vs. dimensionality. Histogram view of cosine similarities for positive pairs (alignment) and negatives (uniformity), corresponding to Fig. 2. As dimensionality increases, alignment stays high while uniformity improves, pushing negative-pair similarities toward zero. The middle panel is a zoom of the left; the right panel highlights that with very small batch sizes, increasing dimensionality offers limited uniformity improvement.

color.semantic_mapping: Five colors encode dimensions 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512; black arrows/text identify uniformity and alignment.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: right side shared across the three panels

encodings.facet: batch=128 full view; batch=128 zoom; batch=8 low-batch view
encodings.text: Batch-size labels and arrows for uniformity/alignment

figures.data_and_statistics: Positive-pair and negative-pair cosine-similarity distributions across dimensions 32–512. The high-batch panels show negative similarities moving toward zero while alignment stays high; the batch=8 panel retains the limited-dimensionality-gain boundary. No error bars or run uncertainty are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix alternate visualization of Figure 2's dimensionality sweep; it complements Figure 7 and tests the same plateau/uniformity story under a different control variable.
design_strengths: The paired zoom and low-batch panel expose both trend and limit.
The figure keeps the positive alignment peak visible while inspecting negative-pair spread.
The shared legend maps all five dimensions consistently.
design_weaknesses: Five overlapping fills are difficult to separate near zero.
No shape or line-style redundancy protects the dimension encoding.
The repeated figure grammar adds space without adding uncertainty or n.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched histogram panels for a primary sweep, a zoom, and a limiting condition; keep the axes and visual semantics identical across the pair of figures.

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Whitening and uniformity: unnormalized representations. Cosine similarity histograms of negatives for CLIP (image, text) and DINO, before (raw) and after whitening. Unnormalized representations benefit from whitening, with distributions pushed closer to zero, reflecting enhanced uniformity. The y-axis (“Density”) represents the relative count in each bin (normalized by the total number of samples) rather than the probability density function.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue fill is Raw, coral fill is Whitened, and black is axes/direct model labels; CLIP image/text and DINO are named in-panel.

figures.data_and_statistics: Negative cosine-similarity histograms for unnormalized CLIP image/text and DINO representations before and after whitening. Density is a total-sample-normalized bin count, not a probability-density function. No uncertainty interval or repetition is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Paired with Figure 10 and Table 2 to support the post-hoc whitening extension; the object tests a distributional mechanism, not the core InfoNCE theorem.
design_strengths: Raw/Whitened overlay makes the movement toward zero direct.
The caption defines the nonstandard Density y-axis.
Three models share one compact comparison layout.
design_weaknesses: Repeated legends add clutter and color is not redundant.
No numeric uniformity effect or sample count accompanies the shape comparison.
Different panel peak heights invite cross-model comparisons despite independent scales.
figures.reusable_pattern: Overlay pre/post transformation distributions for each model and define the histogram normalization in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 10

caption.text: Whitening and uniformity: normalized representations. Cosine similarity histograms of negatives for CLIP (image, text) and DINO, before (normalized) and after whitening. Normalized representations are already close to uniform; whitening provides a modest but consistent improvement.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue fill is normalized/raw and coral fill is whitened; black is axes/direct model text.

figures.data_and_statistics: Negative cosine-similarity count histograms for normalized CLIP image/text and DINO representations before and after whitening. The three panels use scientific-notation count scales; no error bars, n annotation, or repeated-run uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Normalized counterpart to Figure 9; together they support the Appendix E.2 claim that whitening gives a modest uniformity improvement even when normalized representations are already near uniform.
design_strengths: It preserves Figure 9's layout, making the normalization comparison economical.
The baseline-near-uniform and modest-improvement message is visually clear.
Model labels and state legend are repeated locally.
design_weaknesses: Count multipliers differ by panel, limiting direct peak-height comparison.
Caption does not explain the scientific-notation multipliers.
Color-only Raw/Whitened encoding is vulnerable in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep a normalized counterpart visually isomorphic to the unnormalized plot and change only the condition being compared.

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: Encoder “pushforward”. On synthetic data, the encoder maps Laplace-distributed inputs to approximately Gaussian representations. Because both source and target families admit tractable likelihoods, we can score entire sets and observe consistently high correlation across different augmentation strengths.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue points are set-level likelihood pairs, red is the trend/reference line, purple marks ρ, and black text/axes identify scores and correlations.

encodings.color: point cloud versus red reference/trend line

figures.data_and_statistics: Synthetic Laplace input and approximately Gaussian embedding likelihood scores across three augmentation correlations. The panels report Pearson/Spearman pairs .87/.86, .86/.85, and .87/.86. The scatter shows ranking correlation, not density calibration or a regression interval.
figures.evidence_relation: Adds a likelihood-ordering view to the Gaussian representation claim and connects to the paragraph following Figure 10; high correlation is support for pushforward ordering, not proof of equal source/target densities.
design_strengths: Shared axes and a common red line support cross-ρ comparison.
Pearson/Spearman annotations make the evidence quantity visible without lookup.
The point cloud exposes dispersion rather than hiding all variation in one score.
design_weaknesses: Dense points and no uncertainty band make the relationship appear more exact than measured.
Caption does not define the score sample unit or report n.
The word “pushforward” can be read causally despite a correlation-only diagnostic.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use parameter-faceted score–score scatters with the key correlation directly annotated, and state that the object supports ordering rather than equality.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Gaussianity diagnostics across data and training settings. We report norm concentration (CV) and Gaussianity via AD and DP tests (average statistic and fraction of compliant coordinates). Lower AD and higher DP indicate closer Gaussian agreement. Binary E0/E50/E100 denote evaluation at epochs 0/50/100; other results are from the end of training. Results use unnormalized embeddings.

tables.uncertainty: No ± values, interval, SD/SE, or error bars. AD/DP rows are average coordinate-wise statistics and fractions passing the stated thresholds; the ✓/× row is a derived decision, not uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Synthetic Linear columns compare Laplace, GMM, and Binary E0/E50/E100; CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 columns compare supervised and contrastive training. CV, AD, DP, compliance fractions, and Gaussian? are reported as endpoint/epoch summaries.
tables.evidence_relation: Quantifies Figure 3's synthetic diagnostics and Figure 4's training story, while placing the supervised-versus-contrastive objective control on the same decision surface.
design_strengths: One compact table combines radial, coordinate-wise, and final decision quantities.
Binary epoch columns retain optimization progression.
Threshold direction is visible in metric/header text and caption.
design_weaknesses: Mean statistics and pass fractions hide coordinate heterogeneity.
Colored ✓/× symbols lose meaning in grayscale without the text row label.
Gaussian? can be overread as a joint-normality guarantee.
tables.reusable_pattern: Combine structural metrics, test statistics, compliance rates, and a final decision row; define direction and time conditions in the caption.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Gaussianity diagnostics for pretrained models. Coordinate-wise Gaussianity via AD and DP tests (average statistic and fraction of compliant coordinates). Test thresholds are indicated in headers. Results shown for Unnormalized / Normalized embeddings.

tables.uncertainty: No ± values, intervals, or error bars. Each AD/DP pair is an average statistic and compliant-coordinate fraction for unnormalized/normalized embeddings; ✓/× is a threshold-derived decision.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows compare supervised ResNet-34/DenseNet with self-supervised DINO/CLIP across MS-COCO and CLIP Image Sketch/Painting. AD and DP values are paired as Unnormalized / Normalized, with threshold labels in the column headers.
tables.evidence_relation: Extends the main claim from synthetic/CIFAR settings to pretrained models, and supplies the tabular reference for Figure 6's radius comparison and Figures 9–10's whitening extension.
design_strengths: Nested AD/DP headers keep thresholds adjacent to their metrics.
Normalized and unnormalized results are paired in every cell.
Training-family row groups make the negative-control direction visible.
design_weaknesses: Mixed decimal precision and scientific notation increase scan cost.
Color-only ✓/× encoding is not grayscale-safe.
Coordinate-wise diagnostics remain a proxy for the joint Gaussian claim.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use grouped model rows with paired raw/normalized metric columns and thresholds embedded in headers to make a broad diagnostic comparison self-contained.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 states the Gaussian-representation headline; Figure 2 maps theory to alignment/uniformity; Figure 3 combines synthetic radial and coordinate diagnostics; Figure 4 shows the CIFAR training trajectory; Tables 1–2 quantify endpoint and pretrained comparisons; Appendix Figures 5–11 add theory intuition, model breadth, whitening and likelihood-ordering checks.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions begin with a bold short title, then describe setup, encoding and directional finding. Figures 7–10 explicitly identify zoom, state and axis semantics; Table 1 defines metric direction and epoch conditions; Table 2 places thresholds in headers but leaves joint-Gaussian scope to the body.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 separates Synthetic (Linear) and CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18) groups; Table 2 nests AD/DP average and compliance subcolumns and pairs Unnormalized/Normalized values. Both terminate in a Gaussian? decision column.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 and Figures 7–8 operationalize alignment plateau and uniformity; Figures 3–4 and Table 1 test thin-shell/normality predictions and the supervised control; Table 2 and Figures 6, 9–11 extend the diagnostic mechanism to pretrained models, whitening and likelihood ordering.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main text points to Appendix E.1/E.2 for implementation and extra plots, to Figures 7–8 for alternate views, and to Appendix D for the exact plateau-bound extension visualized in Figure 5. Appendix objects extend conditions without replacing the main evidence chain.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: NimbusRomNo9L/Times-like body and caption typography is stable; chart labels use a recurring handwritten Kristen-like style, with some later labels available as PDF KristenITC/CambriaMath objects. Size and raster/vector provenance vary by object.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue, green, red and purple recur for model or condition identity, while Figure 2–3 introduce gradients and multiple categorical factors. Most semantic distinctions rely on color without shape/line redundancy; direct labels partly mitigate this.

most_reusable_patterns: Pair complementary mechanism quantities on one setting axis (Figure 2).
Chain global radial structure, raw distributions and coordinate tests in one composite (Figure 3).
Use matched zoom and limiting-condition panels to preserve both the main trend and its boundary (Figures 7–8).
Put thresholds in table headers and pair normalized/unnormalized values in adjacent columns (Tables 1–2).
failure_patterns: No figure/table reports error bars, intervals, seed variation or sample counts.
Color-only semantics have limited grayscale and color-vision robustness.
Coordinate-wise AD/DP and CV proxies can be mistaken for a joint Gaussianity proof.
Figure 1 and Figure 5 use strong geometric metaphors without calibrated axes; Figure 6 and Figure 10 use panel-specific y scales.
The public repository lacks complete Figure 2–11 plotting scripts, leaving many appendix panels non-reconstructible from source.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper compresses an alignment-ceiling → spherical-uniformity → thin-shell/coordinate-diagnostic → pretrained/whitening story into a handwritten, color-coded main/appendix sequence, with interpretation limited by missing uncertainty and joint-distribution diagnostics.
